text: The Patriots are making moves on both the roster and the ceremonial front this week: they've released LB Jose Ramirez while signing CB Al'Zillion Hamilton to the practice squad and parting ways with OL Da'Metrius Weatherspoon, all as they prepare to honor Pro Football Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri during halftime against the Raiders on October 11. After Drake Maye's clutch performance lifted New England past Buffalo 29-26 in Week 4—snapping a disappointing early-season stretch and pushing the Patriots to 2-2—the team now faces a stiff test against Las Vegas's dangerous tight end duo of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer following their success neutralizing Dalton Kincaid. The Week 4 comeback win appears to have arrested what looked like a troubling slide for the defending AFC champions, with analysts dissecting how Maye and the offense finally broke out against Josh Allen's Bills and debating whether the Patriots' rally is genuine or merely an overreaction to one win. Head Coach Mike Vrabel emphasized the critical nature of the victory, one that was part of a broader pattern of Week 4 comebacks—alongside the Rams and Cowboys—that may have kept several teams' seasons from derailing completely.
